rubric.result: The seven sentences of `### Desired end state`, each against the accumulated diff. (1) `POST /coordinating-session` confirms the checkout, resolves the idea, writes the phase prompt, installs the hooks and spawns `claude` with no worktree and no branch: `open-coordinating-session.ts` runs `workspace.confirm` -> `userStories.detail` (only when a story was given) -> `conversations.mint` -> `PhasePrompt.brainstorming` -> `records.prepare` -> `sessionHooks.install` -> `conversations.start`, and `workspace.prepare` is never called; the route is mounted in `api-server.ts` and every adapter is wired in `ct-api.ts`. (2) The prompt never travels as text: `ClaudeConversations` puts `CT_PHASE_PROMPT` in the spawned environment on `start` only, and the single argument is `OPENING = 'Read the file at "$CT_PHASE_PROMPT" and do exactly what it says.'`, expanded by the login shell (`argv: ['-il', '-c', command]`), so no prompt text reaches the argv. (3) `POST /session-hooks` projects the three events: `UserPromptSubmit` -> `working()`, `Notification` -> `waiting(message)`, `Stop` -> `waiting(null)`, and `SessionAttention.working()` carries `question === null`, which is the question being dropped the moment the session works again. (4) The purge: `LocalSettingsSessionHooks.install` rebuilds each of the three events from `#purged(hooks[event])` — dropping only entries whose command contains the `CT_SESSION_HOOKS_URL` marker — and spreads `...settings` and `...existing`, so foreign hooks and foreign events survive. (5) `GET /coordinating-session` answers `none`, `live` (with `attention.status` and `attention.question`) or `unresumable` with its detail. (6) Start-up recall: `RecoverCoordinatingSession.execute` reads the record, answers `none`, `unresumable` without asking `resume` or `start`, or resumes; `ct-api.ts` runs it after `server.start()` (the hooks url needs the port) and remembers the outcome with one stderr line either way. (7) The entrance keeps its four fields and its one button (`Arrancar brainstorming`, calling `CoordinatingSessionClient.open` with the unchanged `StartPlanSubmission`), and `Home.tsx` holds one `<section className="home__sessions">` with `SessionsPanel` and `CoordinatingSessionStatus` as a sibling of the workspace section, outside every `currentStage` branch and with nothing disabled; `SessionsPanel` lists every live session, so the `brainstorming` terminal is reachable and writable in the review and implementation stages too. Nothing the end state promises is absent, and no promise one commit carried was undone by a later one. One residue is the finding below: the entrance still tells the person that a plan is being prepared while the button opens a conversation. The unguarded `await recoverCoordinatingSession.execute()` in `ct-api.ts` is not counted here — it is already on record as the judge's `low` on task 9 and declared in `backend/API.md` lines 811-816 and in the plan's assumption 15.

Fourteen task commits in order (plus one merge of `origin/main` carrying #319's harvest ledger, which is why `plugin/` and `docs/loop/` appear in `## Files changed` — none of that is this slice's work). Each commit leaves the previous ones standing and the two reversals are both asked for by the objective of the task that makes them: task 13 turns task 6's `ConversationNotRecorded`-for-a-malformed-record into `ConversationNotUnderstood` ('an unreadable record stops being reported as a failed write') and rewrites task 4's composed argv assertion into a literal ('the argv assertion stops being built from the constants it measures'), and both carry their `PlanCollapse` row, so nothing task 2 established is left without one. No scaffolding for an intermediate state survives: the state task 1 removed from `PtyLiveSessions` (`shell`, `cwd`, `env`) left with its only reader, and the `planStarted` / `planStartUncertain` / `uncertain-start` branch task 12 deleted is exactly what lost its caller when task 11 stopped starting a plan — plan assumption 8 names that removal and the review and implementation stages keep their restore path. Nothing is solved twice in two different ways: task 8's event vocabulary is built from task 5's `LocalSettingsSessionHooks.EVENTS` rather than re-listed, and task 7's `PlanRequest.from` is reused instead of a second parser. `frontend/src/app/start-plan/client.ts` losing its last caller is closed by D-26 and by task 11's brief, not a drift. One duplication lives only in the relationship between task 1 and task 4 and is the `low` below.

Signal declared: 'the session status moves from working to waiting and the live question is readable in the cabin'. (a) Production code emits it, end to end and outside any test: `LocalSettingsSessionHooks.COMMAND` installs the three hooks in the checkout's `.claude/settings.local.json`, `ClaudeConversations` puts `CT_SESSION_HOOKS_URL` into the spawned environment pointing at the listening port (`ct-api.ts`, `hooksUrl`), `SessionHooksRoute.handledBy` projects the payload onto `SessionAttention`, `CoordinatingSessions.attend` replaces the held attention, `GET /coordinating-session` answers `attention: {status, question}`, and `CoordinatingSessionStatus.tsx` renders `Trabajando` / `Esperando` / `Te está preguntando: <question>` inside the `home__sessions` section that `Home.tsx` keeps on the page in every phase — that is the cabin reading it. The tests over this chain sit on top of production lines, they are not where the signal lives. (b) With the repo's own instrumentation: this backend has no logging library in `backend/package.json` (`express` and `node-pty` are the only dependencies) and emits through an injected `stderr` collaborator; the slice uses that same one — `coordinating-sessions.ts:59` writes `coordinating session ${conversation} ${attention.status}` beside the existing `pty-live-sessions.ts:73` `live session ${session.id} (${program.name}) opened`, and `ct-api.ts` hands it `(line) => process.stderr.write(line)` exactly as every other collaborator there receives it. Nothing new was brought in. (c) Every dimension bounded: the projected status is `AttentionStatus`, a frozen pair `working` / `waiting`, `CoordinatingSessionState` is the frozen pair `live` / `unresumable`, and the recovery outcome is the frozen `none` / `live` / `unresumable`; the free-text `question` is the payload the signal exists to make readable, carried in the answer's body and on screen, not a label or dimension anything is grouped by, and the conversation id appears only interpolated into a log sentence, which is this repository's established shape for the same fact. No smell either: the cell names something read in production after the merge — a person watching the cabin flip from `Trabajando` to `Esperando` with the question under `Te está preguntando`, plus the stderr transition line — so it is not an acceptance criterion restated, and `plugin/conventions/simplicity.md`'s question ('who reads this, and where?') is answered by the human at `http://127.0.0.1:8787` and by whoever reads the backend's terminal.

findings.what: The entrance was repurposed and one of its own paragraphs still describes the work the button no longer does. While the form is sending — which now means `POST /coordinating-session`, i.e. a `claude` spawned in the governed checkout with no worktree cut, no branch created and no repository check run — the page tells the person that preparing the plan can take several minutes while the repository's checks run, and not to close the page or send it again. The end state's last sentence keeps the four fields and the one button and says the button now opens the brainstorming; the sum of the fourteen commits delivers that (the literal is `Arrancar brainstorming`, the sending label `Abriendo el brainstorming`, the call `CoordinatingSessionClient.open`) and leaves this paragraph beside them contradicting it. No task's objective named it: task 11's brief froze `the locked summary, the field validation, the refusal banner and the start-plan-help text`, and this is `start-plan-form__pending`, which no sentence of the plan mentions either way, so no per-task judge had it in view — task 14's `low` is about `frontend/README.md`'s stale intro, a different artefact, and this one is not recorded in the plan's §9 nor in `backend/API.md`. Medium rather than high because nothing the slice promised is missing and nothing is broken: it is Spanish product copy that misinforms the person for the seconds the button is in flight, and the repair is one sentence in one file.

findings.what: Two commits write the same rule twice. Task 1 moved the environment filtering out of `PtyLiveSessions.open` into `static #definedEntriesOf` (`pty-live-sessions.ts:140`), where it builds the login shell's `SessionProgram`; task 4 needed the same filtering to build the conversation's `SessionProgram` and, because that static is private, copied it verbatim into `claude-conversations.ts:108` — same name, same signature, same six lines, one `SessionProgram.env` consumer each. Neither objective mentions the other's copy: task 1's stops at the login shell and task 4's at the CLI's environment, which is why this is visible only between the two commits and not inside either. Low: the duplicated code is a pure filter with no rule of the domain in it, and both copies feed the same value object, so nothing can drift apart in behaviour; whoever closes it does so by making the helper reachable once (on `SessionProgram`, where the field it fills lives) and deleting the second copy.
